newsitem.title: GERMANY: Low rapemeal demand drags down N.Europe seed price.
newsitem.headline: Low rapemeal demand drags down N.Europe seed price.

text.p: Rapeseed prices in Northern Europe are drifting lower because demand for rapeseed meal is falling, brokers said on Friday.

They said rapemeal sellers were unable to place material for autumn and winter dates when buyers were expecting to have a wide choice of competing feed grains and so-called mid-proteins, for example palmkernel products and corngluten.
Reports of favourable grain and oilseeds weather both sides of the Atlantic also supported the negative price trend.
Apart from supply pressure, good growing weather in Europe means farmers can cut grass for silage, which reduces their requirements for bought-in feeds.
New crop buyers for ex-harvest seed were at 430 marks/tonne free Hamburg, 10 marks down on the week.
French rapeseed offers in west German markets were also weighing on prices.
Rapeseed prices for delivery at points other than Hamburg were in a 422.50-437.50 marks range for July/August compared with 427.50-440 marks quoted last week.
November rapeseed on the Matif futures traded at 432 marks, down five from Thursday's close and off 10 on the week.
July rape meal was steady at 29.75 marks/100 kg while August-October meal stood at 23.75 marks and November/January at 24.75.
Rape oil sellers' prices were down at 93.75 marks on July (off 1.25) and August/October was off 1.75 at 90.50.
